question: Can we design a bacterium that eats carbon, and could it live anywhere?

generations.asked: a bacterium that eats carbon and swims
generations.what_it_taught: The request names no organism the tool can read, and the tool now says so instead of building an animal. "Bacterium" is not a taxon word in this repository; a scientific name is the way in.

generations.asked: Cupriavidus necator that fixes carbon dioxide and swims
generations.what_it_taught: A scientific name now resolves, the clade table reaches bacteria, and a declared parameter set resolves a STATE, so a prokaryote gets all the way into the studio, the law check and organism_get. What it finds there is that the anatomy ontologies, the cell ontology and the law set are all animal artefacts. The pipeline is clade-general; its contents are not.

generations.asked: the same organism, swimming with a hinged paddle
generations.what_it_taught: IMPOSSIBLE, by a theorem rather than a simulation. At Re of order 1e-5 a time-reversible stroke returns the body exactly where it began, so the paddle design does not move slowly: it does not move. This is a verdict no shape-only layer could ever have reached, because nothing is wrong with the paddle as a structure.

generations.asked: the same organism, swimming with a rotating helical flagellum
generations.what_it_taught: The theorem no longer binds it and the declared cycle is consistent with the declared speed. That is NOT a finding that it swims: there is no motor model, no torque, no energy budget and no control here. It is the absence of a contradiction, which is the most this layer is able to offer.

generations.asked: could this organism establish anywhere, against what is already there
generations.what_it_taught: On the designer's own four numbers the strain cannot invade when rare: at the resident guild's carrying capacity its per-capita growth rate is negative, so it is excluded. That outcome is a property of those four numbers and not a measurement of anything, and the run says so twice. What the real databases contribute is the other half: where the clade is actually recorded, what is actually in the chosen box, and what is actually recorded as interacting with it -- facts with studies behind them, and no population parameter anywhere among them.

The request is answerable at last. The first numbers the designer proposed claimed more carbon leaving as biomass and CO2 than entered, which conservation of mass forbids outright -- and the check said impossible rather than unlikely. Corrected, the balance holds at a 55 percent yield. What the check still cannot say is everything about whether the organism could do it: no transporter kinetics, no energy budget, and carbon fixation is expensive in ATP rather than in carbon.

verdict: The request is answerable at last. Corrected, the balance holds at a 55 percent yield. What the check still cannot say is everything about whether the organism could do it: no transporter kinetics, no energy budget, and carbon fixation is expensive in ATP rather than in carbon.
headline: Asked for a bacterium, the blueprint tool used to build an animal. Asked to swim with a paddle, the locomotion layer returns impossible by theorem. Asked whether it could live somewhere, the ecology layer assembles real records and refuses to predict exclusion from them. And asked whether it eats carbon -- which is the whole request, and reached no check at all until this round -- the mass balance says the first numbers proposed were impossible, and says which atoms were missing.
